operations.comment: ; Round003 contextual aliases; banked table addresses require the documented bank2 view.
; Shared CPU RAM and Sega mapper aliases. RAM mirrors at E000-FFFF; mapper registers override FFFC-FFFF.
; Shared 48-byte object-record offsets, established by motion/animation consumers.
; Audio has independent 32-byte channel records; never use gameplay object fields here.
; Bank15 CPU aliases for pointer data; raw-data WLA sections use physical placement slots.
; CPU-space RAM symbols. Coordinate words use8.8 fixed point where the consumers shift by8.
; Camera integer aliases intentionally overlap fixed-point words; hardware and backing identities remain separate.
; Bonus aliases share RAM with legacy palette-service and exit-copy aliases; use
; the name belonging to the current consumer rather than inferring one global role.
; Reset jumps to the interrupt-disabled machine initialization entry.

; Drive both controller TH outputs high, then low, and compare the corresponding input bits. Return FF only when both readings follow the driven level, otherwise zero. Initialization saves this capability result; the board/region interpretation remains tentative.
; Uniform FF bytes between independent vector routines; no additional purpose is inferred.
; IM1 jumps to the frame interrupt handler. The handler itself is reviewed separately.
; VDP register setup begins at CPU003B: startup emits22 bytes with OTIR. Remaining bounded initialization bytes and FF run are retained as data; no additional schema is inferred.
; Pause NMI preserves AF. Only session flag pattern 04 permits a toggle; a 15-frame debounce
; prevents immediate retriggering. Toggle the pause latch and clear its debounce counter.
; Initialize stack and IM1, then map ROM bank 6 into the 8000 window.

; Continue reset with audio quieting, low-RAM clearing and the DF-port setup. A bounded nested addition loop provides settling time before the TH-line and FM probes. Disable interrupts again, reset SP, acknowledge VDP status and stream the 22-byte register setup. Clear gameplay RAM, fill the palette buffer, map bank 2 and expand the font source to VRAM 2000. Select initial mode 80 and enable display interrupts before falling through to the main loop. Calls into window 2 require the effective mapped bank; they do not establish a persistent bank contract.
; signed -1 for the settling-delay addition
; Service the frame synchronization helper, then dispatch through nine little-endian CPU words.
; Push this entry as the handler return address; the low mode nibble selects an unchecked word.
; The observed mode contract keeps the index within the table; this fragment does not enforce it.
; DispatchMainMode indexes by MainMode low nibble; nine little-endian CPU addresses in fixed ROM.
; mode 0
; mode 1
; mode 2
; mode 3
; mode 4
; mode 5
; mode 6
; mode 7
; mode 8
; Mode bit 7 enables this input path. Preserve a return continuation on the stack,
; sample controller state and recognize newly changed action-button bits 30.
; Mode 41 becomes 03; other eligible modes enter 86. The last-button latch suppresses repeats.
; Calls and raw gaps remain separate physical source ranges.

; Temporarily set memory-control bit 2, then test seven alternating values through F2. Count matching masked readbacks; only seven successes enable the saved FM-present flag. Write the resulting enable bit to F2 and restore the saved memory-control value. This cartridge-enabled static view does not establish execution aliases with the cartridge disabled.
; Only advance an enabled, unfinished input sequence when controller state changes to nonzero.
; Alternate registers preserve the caller state while the sequence counter selects one of six masks.
; A matching masked input sets the completion flag; the precise sequence purpose is unresolved.
; A direct-flow return stub. It changes no registers or state; the following six bytes are button masks.
; Six button masks consumed by the player-button dispatcher, ending at the independent mode-zero entry.

; Initialize mode zero once, map bank 2 into CPU8000, expand the common graphic and upload 35 two-plane tiles plus a 4x10 tile rectangle. Start a 240-tick delay and palette transition; after the shared completion test, advance to mode81.
; Counted palette-transition request consumed by mode-zero initialization.

; Write DE to the VDP control port. The following rectangle writer consumes B rows of C tile bytes, pairs each with the saved attribute A, and advances the VRAM row by64 bytes. Callers must provide valid port timing and nonzero counts.
; Save attribute A and emit B rows of C tile IDs from HL. DE is the VDP destination; each row starts64 VRAM bytes after the previous row.

; Upload B tiles from HL after setting VDP address DE. Each tile has eight rows: emit its two source plane bytes, then two zero planes. Stack exchanges supply the VDP port delays; counts must be nonzero.
; Emit D rows using two source bytes and two zero planes per row; XOR A establishes the cleared planes.
; Presentation values and bounded descriptors between the VDP upload helper and the next routine. Their non-code role is established; exact partition remains unresolved.
; Mode bit 6 is the one-time initialization latch. Already initialized execution branches
; to CPU 0305; the intervening initialization path is retained in source order.

; Finish clearing the mode byte pair and reset the text/display service. Disable interrupts while clearing sprite/game RAM, expanding bank-2 and bank-9 graphics and copying a 12-byte setup block to the stage work area. Select name-table base 3800, re-enable interrupts and tail-call the text writer with CPU 027B. Those source addresses belong to the explicitly selected banks.
; Read the next state byte: substeps 1 and 2 branch to separate handlers.
; Other values initialize a 0600 word in the C70C work area and call the update helper.
; Stage-work flag bit 3 advances the mode delay and starts a 16-step fade with the input-sequence flag set to 80. Return without changes while that bit is clear.
; Decrement the C63F mode counter. Its surrounding handler is not fully classified.

; Continue only when the preceding timer result is zero. Reload six ticks and advance the page index, loading a word from CPU 038A into the display request and arming it with 80. After index 13, wait for the 16-frame condition counter, advance the mode, copy five attract-state bytes, map bank 2 and transfer to its B2E1 continuation.
; Return while the high bit of AttractSequenceFlags remains set; otherwise enter mode 82.
; Tail-call the shared text/display reset service; the caller's return remains on the stack.
; Thirteen paired attract-input values followed by five initial playback-state bytes. The finite input reader and following routine bound the storage.
; Only active sequences run. Select ROM bank 9, then test the page-animation flag.
; A 24-tick timer alternates two destination addresses for a 34-byte update.
; A separate 180-tick timer advances through three page destinations using a word table.
; The last page clears the active flag. The visual meaning of each page is unresolved.
; Immediate return reached from the attract-mode control flow. No state change occurs here.
; Three little-endian pointers selected by the attract-page sequence.
; Set bit 6 in the caller-selected flag byte; its predecessor bytes remain unclassified.

; Upload four fixed tile/name-table spans through the shared VRAM writer, then render two three-byte packed-decimal fields from C040 and C013 at their panel positions. The last decimal-render call is a tail call.
; Bounded presentation values adjacent to mode-two initialization. Consumers establish data; an exact field partition remains unresolved.

; Initialize mode two once, load the bank2 presentation, alternate between two descriptors in bank4, copy the chosen stage plus five playback-state bytes, and start gameplay with session bit4 set. Completed playback advances to mode6; otherwise enter the existing gameplay path.
; Two attract-playback descriptors selected alternately. Each chooses a stage plus five bytes copied to playback state; bank4 contains the referenced controller streams.
; Silence/reset the bank6 sound service, restore the bank2 graphic and display state, clear work RAM C040..DDFF, then select mode81 with no delay.
; Bounded mode/presentation descriptors after the reset routine; exact subfields remain unresolved.
; Initialize this mode once; clear C028-DDFF while retaining the mode/input header.
; Reset stage selection to zero. Session input-sequence flags choose the alternate selector path.
; ROM bank 5 is selected for the following presentation transfer.
; Copy the selector presentation, then poll at a one-tick cadence and suppress held inputs.
; Direction bit 0 decrements with wrap from 0 to 18; the other direction increments modulo 19.
; Each choice addresses a 16-byte presentation row at BE00 + index*16 in ROM bank 5.
; An action button takes a continuation beyond this classified fragment.
; Finish the caller-prepared VRAM transfer, enable interrupts and return. Source, destination and count are supplied by the preceding setup.
; Disable interrupts for display setup, select bank 2 and unpack the fixed stream
; at CPU 8395 to VRAM 2160. Enter mode 8 and reset several work counters.
; The game meanings of C07A/C044/C0A6-C0A8/C06C-C06D remain unresolved.
; Session bits 0 and 1 divert to death/clear-like continuations. Otherwise run the
; frame object/display helpers, select bank 2 and call its ADAF helper.
; Decrement GameplayCountdown only when nonzero. Calls alone do not establish hidden helper semantics.
; Write request 86 to DE03 and clear work flag C07C bit 6. The request consumer
; needs further review before assigning a game-specific name.

; Mark the current flag byte, arm the transition byte and wait 240 frames through the condition service. Issue sound request 09, clear session bits 0 and 2, then decrement the signed HUD/life counter. A nonnegative result selects mode 5; exhaustion selects mode 7. Both paths join the existing mode-transition setup.
; Write request 88. C652 bit 2 selects an alternate presentation that hides the sprite
; list with the D0 terminator and sets work byte C614. Clear C07C bit 6 in either case.
; Set the current flag's high bit, arm the transition state and initialize the 240-frame condition counter. This fragment continues into the shared frame-wait path below.
; Wait through frame synchronization until the condition helper returns zero.
; Issue helper request 9, clear nine stage-progress bytes C093-C09B and clear session bit 1.
; Session bit 7 selects an alternate continuation. Artificial clear experiments confirm this path,
; not natural victory or an ending.

; Initialize the bonus scene, request sound 82 and set the service countdown. Each frame checks the bonus completion bit, services shooting input and wave spawning, updates objects, then explicitly maps bank 2 for its target-collision scan. Loop until completion, seed the bonus cursor state, issue request 02 and enter bonus score conversion. This is the shooting bonus path; it does not establish an ending or credits route.
; C652 bit 2 selects an object-completion wait before advancing the stage.
; Increment StageIndex; choose mode 8 while the result is at most 18, otherwise mode 7.
; Restore the C06C counter from C06D on the alternate path and tail-call the shared reset helper.
; Clear the C100-D7FF work area and prepare display state with interrupts disabled.
; Unpack fixed four-plane RLE assets from bank 2 to VRAM 2000 and 2160, then
; bank 4 CPU 9780 to VRAM 02C0. Each consumer advances its source to the stream terminator.
; In bank 15, index B2B7 by StageIndex*3. Each record is one effective ROM bank
; followed by a little-endian stream pointer. Select that bank and unpack to VRAM 2800.
; The descriptor domain is 19 records; stream validation established four equal output planes.
; Run stage support initializers, then initialize scroll/control work bytes and terminate
; the sprite-Y list with D0. Re-enable interrupts. In bank 2, select a stage word
; from CPU 86B0 into C0A4, then switch to bank 9 for object parameters.
; In ROM bank 9, stage-indexed word tables initialize primary-object bytes C1C3/C1C6
; and C09C. A byte selector chooses one of four-byte parameter records copied to C09E-C0A1.
; C652 bit 2 chooses request 87 instead of 81; precise request semantics remain unresolved.
; Store the selected request in DE03. In ROM bank 9, a stage word from AAF0
; yields a resource pointer; skip its first byte and submit it with bank value 9.
; Set session bit 2. If bit 3 is clear, enter gameplay mode 4; otherwise preserve
; the caller-selected main mode. This is the supported artificial-stage initialization contract.
; Tile-transfer descriptor consumed by ApplyTransferList, ending exactly at the next routine.
; Select ROM bank 9 and copy seven bytes from an eight-byte stage record into C64C-C652.
; Select bank 15, initialize the source/destination work pointers and scroll state.
; Stage 14 uses the special coordinate setup below.
; For stage 14, use the alternate C928 work destination and establish the special
; coordinate words and mode byte before joining ordinary stage-parameter setup.
; Index bank-15 table B2F0 by StageIndex*2, then copy sixteen parameter bytes
; into C71C-C72B. C700 bit 4 chooses the coordinate conversion below.
; Negate the low coordinate byte to extract its tile-phase bit. Add the C719
; and C71B words with carry into C71D, then retain the upper coordinate bytes.
; Extract bit 3 into C708, divide the C71C coordinate by sixteen and store
; its low result in C709, then jump into the shared coordinate continuation.

; Clear the forward-section request and increment the section index. Map bank 9, select the stage camera table through AA72, then index four-byte section entries and copy the selected coordinate word to both camera targets. The trailing reverse entry clears the opposite request and decrements the index before joining the existing shared lookup.
; In ROM bank 9, choose a stage pointer from AA72. A four-byte subrecord indexed
; by C71E supplies two little-endian words copied to C728 and C72A.
; In bank 15, copy a 78-byte stage sprite-resource list into RAM D520. Its first
; byte counts entries. Each entry selects an effective bank, an RLE source word and
; a VRAM destination word. A following optional count/pointer requests a bit-reversed
; VRAM copy. This is the consumer behind the independently validated counted lists.
; Scan nine stage-progress bytes. Zero slots are skipped; nonzero slots retain
; only bits 4F. The precise progression meaning of those bits is still unresolved.
; Select bank 9, read the stage word from AE6E and copy nine bytes into
; StageProgressSlots. These are the slots cleared and normalized by the stage-clear path.

; Consumer-referenced/repeated fixed-window table, palette, tile or offset storage. Role inspected in the bounded reference/consumer review; generic non-code for unresolved partition or complete selector domain.
; Mode bit 6 prevents repeated initialization. Disable interrupts, set VDP register 0,
; clear C100-DDFF and prepare the fixed bank-2 graphics. Apply the presentation descriptor
; at CPU 0A86, set a 300-tick condition counter and queue the palette at 0A9D.
; This artificial route was observed at GAME OVER; a genuine ending remains unproven.

; User-directed generic unclassified DATA physical [3173,3176), Manual confidence 0. Original structural role remains UNKNOWN; prior alternate-entry/data ambiguity is unresolved. Exact bytes retained; this choice is not non-code or reachability proof.
; Either controller action button can finish this screen. Otherwise decrement the
; 16-bit condition counter and return until it reaches zero. Clear the button latch
; before the exit setup and deferred mode selection.
; Store 81 as the main mode and return; the main mode service handles its deferred transition.
; Set session bit 2 and initialize this mode only once. Clear sprite/object working
; memory, seed the primary object and animation-table pointers, then select a stage
; presentation rectangle. The duplicated pointer writes are original behavior.
; Bank selections are explicit; the initial bank-2 pointer table must be read before switching.
; Load the bank-5 RLE presentation, then use the stage palette word. The later
; path waits for PrimaryObjectFlags to clear, enters stage-initialization mode 5
; and submits the same stage palette through the transition helper.

; Three19-word little-endian pointer arrays: stage graphics, raw32-byte palettes, and stage resources. StageIndex0..18 supplies the finite domain. Graphics/palettes use bank5; raw palettes are distinct from counted palette requests.
; Clear the frame-completion byte, service the pause helper if paused, then wait
; until the interrupt increments it. The pause loop re-enters at the pause test.

; Map audio bank 6 and mute it, then wait for FrameCompleted. Consume each frame flag and update objects while pause remains set. Continue waiting until the pause latch clears, then return. The loop depends on frame interrupts rather than a CPU busy-delay duration.
; Fill 0380 words at VRAM 3800 with the word stored at CPU 0C02, then fill
; 64 bytes at VRAM 3F00 with the byte at CPU 0C04. These are name/sprite-table resets.
; Decrement the C615 16-bit counter and return Z when it reaches zero.
; There is no saturation: callers must stop decrementing after completion.
; HL points to a count followed by transfer records: destination word, byte count
; word and that many inline bytes. Transfer each payload to VRAM and advance over it.
; Multiply the initial H byte by E using eight shift/add steps; return the
; unsigned 16-bit product in HL. D is cleared before the accumulator loop.

; Multiply BC by the original DE with sixteen shift/add steps. DE:HL receives the unsigned32-bit product; A is the loop counter. The carry from each low-word addition increments the high word. Caller and natural reachability remain unknown.

; Run 16 restoring-division steps with DE supplying the shifting dividend/quotient and HL the remainder; BC is the divisor. Carry from the shift or a successful subtraction sets the quotient bit by incrementing E. A failed subtraction restores HL. No zero-divisor guard is supplied here.
; Session bit 2 enables sampling. Bit 4 selects another input route outside this
; classified fragment; ordinary sampling preserves the previous state before reading controller 1.
; Use the established controller reader and store its result in C603. No caller is established for this wrapper.
; Return active-high six-button controller-1 bits by inverting port DC and masking 3F.
; Combine controller-2 bits split across DC and DD, invert to active-high
; and return six button/direction bits. RL C supplies the two DC bits to RLA.
; Select bank 4 for the prerecorded input-sequence interpreter below.

; Interpret the bank-4 prerecorded controller sequence through IX=C00B. Positive counts repeat one controller byte; counts with bit 7 set select a literal run of low-seven-bit length. IX+1 is the position/count and IX+3/+4 the stream pointer. Advance to the next record when its count is exhausted; a zero record sets the sequence's completion bit. GameplayController and ControllerState receive the repeated form; the literal form updates GameplayController as encoded.
; Read VDP status; non-frame interrupts branch to a separate fragment. Save both
; register sets, index registers and the current 8000-window bank. Sample console reset
; on DD bit 4 and detect a falling edge using the previous sample. Bank 6 serves that path.
; Call the current window-2 audio reset entry, then jump to fixed CPU 00BA for machine initialization. The caller must provide the matching audio-bank view for the first call.
; VDP data port is BE. Upload-control C614 bits 7 and 6 choose the display update
; route. When both request it, C63B supplies the ROM bank for the queued pattern upload.
; Set VRAM write address zero and stream 64-byte unrolled chunks from the
; source pointer at C600. C634 is the chunk count; zero would wrap to 256 chunks,
; so valid callers must provide a positive count.
; Upload 64 Y entries from C100 to VRAM 3F00, then 128 X/pattern bytes from
; C140 to VRAM 3F80. Saturate the pause debounce counter at 15. A paused frame
; skips the update chain; otherwise update helpers run according to upload and frame flags.
; The individual object/audio helper semantics remain for their own source review.
; Run the remaining frame helpers, select bank 6 and call CPU 8000. Clear the
; pending upload byte when its high bit is set, increment the frame-completion byte
; and restore the saved 8000-window ROM bank.
; Restore alternate and main registers, both index registers and original AF;
; enable interrupts and return. The original uses RET rather than RETI.
; Begin the horizontal-scroll register write with the work byte at C63A.

; Complete the VDP register-8 write begun above, then set register 10 to 8F. Restore AF, enable interrupts and return. The two-write VDP control protocol makes these bytes part of the scroll update, not an independent data table.
; Begin the scroll register write with the coordinate byte at C70F.
; Complete the VDP register-8 selection and join the shared scroll-register exit above. The relative branch preserves the caller's existing AF save.
; The first entry sets the VRAM write address from HL. CPU 1025 then copies
; BC bytes from DE, preserving DE and BC. A zero count wraps, so callers supply a positive size.
; Copy positive BC bytes from DE to VRAM HL; preserve BC and DE.
; CPU 1036 repeats the byte at DE for BC bytes. CPU 1046 repeats the two-byte
; word at DE for BC words; it uses stack exchanges as port timing delays.
; Repeat the source word at DE for positive BC words.
; HL is destination, DE packed source, B rows and C words per row. Emit both bytes
; of each word, then advance destination by 64 bytes to the next name-table row.
; The inner count is widened to BC with B zero; saved BC restores the row count.
; Set the CRAM command from HL and copy B bytes from DE to the VDP data port.
; Stack exchanges provide the original port timing delay.

; Save the four-bit plane mask A, set VDP address HL, and read BC bytes from DE. Emit each byte four times, replacing disabled planes with zero; alternate registers hold the port and mask loop. Requires valid counts, source bank and VDP access; no caller established.
; Unpack four planes from HL to interleaved VRAM at DE, advancing the base by one
; after each plane. Tag zero ends a plane; low seven tag bits are the run count.
; Bit 7 selects literal bytes; otherwise repeat one source byte. Advance VRAM by
; four per output byte and leave HL at the next plane or stream. The plane helper is CPU 10B8.
; Decode one terminated plane; the outer consumer selects four interleaved planes.

; The first entry repeats the existing transfer service four times with adjacent source starts. The following stream entry reads a nonzero run byte: low seven bits are the count and high bit chooses advancing source versus repeating one byte. Each output writes one VRAM byte, then advances the destination by four. Zero ends the stream. Paired EX(SP),HL operations provide delay while preserving the saved return; they do not consume inline parameters.

; Expand two terminated tagged streams from HL into alternating bytes at DE and DE+1. Each packet uses low7 bits as count: high bit selects advancing literal bytes, otherwise repeat one byte; zero tag returns. The inner writer advances destination by2. Valid stream/count/buffer are caller preconditions; caller unknown.
; Read the next tagged packet; a zero tag ends this plane. Preserve the high-bit literal flag while writing its low7-bit count at destination stride2.
; CPU 1148 copies BC VRAM bytes at DE into RAM HL. CPU 115B reads to D800,
; then reverses each byte bit by bit and writes it to VRAM HL. This supports mirrored
; sprite-pattern resources; the transformation itself is exact even where game purpose varies.
; Read VRAM through the D800 scratch area, reverse bits and write the transformed bytes.

; Read BC VRAM bytes through the established reader into D800 scratch, then reverse each byte bitwise and write it at the original VDP address. Interrupt guards protect address/output accesses. Requires valid count and scratch capacity; no caller established.
; Clear the first sixteen palette work bytes, copy sixteen defaults, then overlay
; a counted palette record from HL. Set C048 bit 7 and wait for its frame consumer
; to clear the request. The count must fit the 32-byte palette buffer.
; Sixteen default palette bytes copied to palette RAM with an explicit16-byte block transfer.
; CPU 11E9 clears the 32-byte palette buffer, queues it and waits. CPU 1205
; tests the palette request then decrements the control byte until zero before uploading
; 32 CRAM bytes. The following C641 path is only partially classified.
; Upload a pending palette during the frame service path.

; Repeat the preceding comparison while it remains nonzero, then load the following selector byte and copy one palette entry through the shared palette helper. HL's preceding scan context is supplied by the text service.
; Remember the bank and DE palette pointer, then walk attenuation levels 4 down
; through 0. Wait eight synchronized frames per level and apply the component clamp helper.
; Reload the saved palette source and walk attenuation levels 0 through 3,
; waiting eight synchronized frames each. Select the saved source bank, copy
; 32 bytes to the palette buffer and restore ROM bank 2 before conversion.
; Apply a saturating attenuation to all 32 packed SMS palette bytes.
; Finish palette component clamping, queue its upload, then enter the object scheduler below.
; C611 selects an object slot through a CPU-word table; C619 rotates the starting
; slot between frames. IX points to the selected record. A zero type skips the slot;
; otherwise dispatch through the type table at CPU 5451, then update animation and
; invoke the bank-2 object helper. Eligible visible objects pass collision helpers
; once before setting field 25 bit 0. After 18 slots, terminate the sprite-Y list
; if fewer than64 entries were emitted and queue its frame upload. Pause skips dispatch.
; Type identities and slot scheduler policy remain unresolved.
; Eighteen little-endian RAM pointers used by UpdateObjectBatch. Each selected slot is a 48-byte object; zero type skips dispatch.
; Use the animation ID to select a word from the C09E table. A nonzero descriptor
; provides frame duration and frame count, followed by frame IDs. Field13 is the
; countdown and field 14 the frame index; advance and wrap it only while unpaused.
; Field25 bit 7 suppresses presentation updates in the following continuation.
; Read the selected frame ID and resolve it through the C0A0 word table.
; Copy its chunk count to C61A, presentation byte to object field 21 and payload
; pointer to C61B. IDs below 79 may replace the queued pattern resource; C602 avoids
; repeated loads. A four-byte descriptor at CPU 1445 provides bank, conversion flag
; and source word. The conversion flag selects the mirrored scratch path.
; For mirrored patterns, reverse each source byte into D200 scratch. Queue the resulting
; source at C600, copy its 64-byte chunk count to C634 and set C614 bit 6.
; The ISR later uploads these chunks to VRAM zero.

; Advance input/output pointers and decrement the remaining conversion-byte count. Rejoin the byte-reversal loop while BC is nonzero, then restore the saved source pointer. This is the missing continuation of the mirrored-pattern scratch conversion.

; Seventy-nine four-byte descriptors: ROM bank, mirror flag and little-endian CPU source. Sprite IDs below $4F select a descriptor; the counted sprite list supplies 64 bytes per pattern chunk. Source and bank identity must be used together.
; C700 flags select forward/reverse coordinate handling. Align the horizontal
; coordinate to eight-pixel cells and derive parallel VRAM/RAM destination pointers.
; Extract the half-cell phase into C732 and divide the selected map coordinate
; by16. Flag bit 0 can bypass this setup into the full-row builder.
; Convert the other axis according to direction bit 4, extracting phase C733.
; Divide its coordinate by16, multiply by the map stride C71F and add the first
; axis and map-base C723. C72C holds the resulting map cursor; C72E points to
; a thirteen-entry column scratch buffer at C739.
; For each of13 map cells, select map bank C722, read its metatile ID and
; index an eight-byte record at C726 in bank C725. Select two word pairs using
; phase C732 and store them in column scratch. Map cursor advances by stride.
; C733 chooses the output pair offset. Stage flag C652 bit 1 inserts the fixed word 3148
; presentation override (bytes 48,31); mark the scroll buffer dirty.
; Build a complete scroll window rather than one column. Direction flags select
; signed coordinate conversion, preserve row phase C732 and column phase C733,
; and compare against prior coordinates through C70A/C70B later in this routine.
; Resolve map cell coordinates and base as for the column path. Select RAM
; buffer C900 or C8C0 from the column phase, compute a64-byte wrap split and
; initialize thirteen output row iterations. Each iteration builds17 metatiles
; into the pair of temporary rows C769 and C7AD.
; For17 cells, read each map ID in bank C722 and copy its eight-byte record
; from bank C725 into two four-byte row buffers. Copy the selected phase of
; the first row into the destination up to its64-byte wrap boundary.
; If the row crosses the64-byte buffer boundary, copy the remainder to its
; wrapped base. Advance one row and repeat the phase-selected split copy for
; the second expanded row. A zero remainder bypasses the second copy.
; Advance map cursor by stride and repeat thirteen rows. Compare old/new
; phase coordinates and set dirty/changed flags, then store the new phase.
; Stage flag C652 bit 1 fills128 words at CE00 with bytes 48,31.
; Retain the relevant scroll flags. Skip rebuilding when direction/state flags
; prohibit it or the coordinate high byte is zero. Otherwise adjust the RAM
; destination by64 bytes when the fine coordinate is nonzero and re-enter
; the scroll-coordinate builder.
; Clear the horizontal pending flag and actual-delta word C7F1. The signed8.8
; delta at C70C updates a24-bit coordinate split across C712/C714. Negative motion
; clamps at zero, records actual displacement and updates the circular C710 coordinate
; modulo0800. Boundary crossings set direction/dirty flags; unrelated pending bits survive.
; Positive horizontal motion clamps to the C720 limit; record the actual delta,
; update the circular coordinate and direction flags, then clear C70C. A boundary
; crossing invokes a tile rebuild. The following entry performs the parallel second-axis
; update from C715, unless scroll-state bit 6 routes to the special handler.
; Apply the signed8.8 C715 delta to the24-bit coordinate C71B/C71D. Clamp
; against C728/C72A according to direction and stop repeated boundary transitions
; with C701 bits 0/1. Apply actual displacement to the display coordinate C717,
; wrapping its high byte moduloE0, and to the circular tile coordinate C719
; modulo0800. Direction changes set C700 bit 4/bit 0 and rebuild pending state.
; Clear C715 after consuming it; retain unresolved game-specific camera policy.
; Code; Static; physical 7377..7380. ScrollFlags bit0 requests rebuilding the dirty column through this tail jump.
; The preceding dirty path jumps back into tile rebuilding. This entry writes
; C70F to VDP register 8 (horizontal scroll), then consumes scroll-buffer bit 7.
; Bit0 chooses a full-window upload; otherwise use the narrow column path.
; Write24 tile words to VRAM at 64-byte row intervals, mirroring each word
; into the RAM tile buffer. Alternate register sets retain the separate VRAM
; destination/source and RAM mirror pointers.
; Copy02C0 pairs of bytes from C900 to VRAM 3880. This uploads the prepared
; tile window; a NOP preserves the original VDP write cadence.
; IX is the primary object. Push the common movement continuation, then dispatch
; special state flags or action/direction buttons in priority order. With no input,
; clear action kind and animation timers and select an idle animation through the
; facing-aware animation helper. Movement and attacks use their own fragments below.
; Dispatch the current player buttons in priority order: action buttons, then directional movement. The encounter offset cycle is a separate routine.
; Set action kind2, choose animation 02 or12 from facing bit 5, and clear animation timers.
; Clear action kind and set horizontal speed 0100. Facing bit 5 selects a direction
; continuation; the classified opposite-facing fragment clears motion bit 0.

; Clear motion flag bit 5, reset both primary animation timers and select sequence CPU 1C15. Continue through the shared player motion update. Bit 5 is the facing selector used by the adjacent left-facing entry.
; Motion flag bit 3 prevents this transition. Otherwise select animation from the
; CPU 1C15 record and tail-call the movement/camera helper.
; Clear action kind and set horizontal speedFF00. Facing selects a continuation;
; the classified opposite-facing path sets motion bit 0. Motion bit 2 can reject the
; transition before animation selection. The adjacent state entries retain the intervening transition.
; Set motion flag bit 5, reset the animation timers and select the same idle transition sequence before the shared player update.
